The top correlate is the container's own creation event (a plausible bad-image/config locus given v1.4, but with no prior version to prove a regression); vm-000006 is listed only as the in-radius host and is ruled out as a cause. Blast radius at incident time was empty (nothing downstream), consistent with an isolated container fault.

Both are correlations tightly aligned with the alert, ranked by directness of mechanism.

report.narrative: Alert latency_high on lb-000003 fired 4.9ms after a genesis window in which all 61 resources were created at t=0 (world_diff: created=61, changed=0, deleted=0). blast_radius(lb-000003, depth=2) at incident time is empty (the lb has no downstream dependents), so the relevant candidates are its upstream routing targets. At incident time lb-000003 is state=draining with healthy_targets=1 of 3: container-000004 is restarting (restarts=3), container-000008 is exited, and only vm-000002 is running — a clear mechanism for elevated latency (reduced healthy capacity). Intersecting the diff with the routing targets, the single real mutation is container-000008's image_tag rollback v1.5 -> v1.4 (seq 13); container-000004 and lb-000003 itself carry only their genesis upserts. Because the lb was seeded already degraded and the one true change (the rollback) left container-000008 exited before and after, no in-window change cleanly explains a new fault — hence no confident candidate. The two dead backends are listed as the best correlates, with container-000008's rollback ranked above the born-broken container-000004.
